summary.description: Benzo(g,h,i)perylene is a colourless, crystal-like solid belonging to the group of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). It is used in the production of drugs, dyes, plastics, pesticides, and explosives, and can also be produced during incomplete combustion.
emission_sources: Natural sources such as forest fires
environmental_impact: Exposure can affect eyes, liver, skin, and immune system
Some PAHs may cause genetic damage and cancer
Can travel long distances in the atmosphere on soot particles, leading to environmental damage far from the emission source

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Benzo(g,h,i)perylene, as a PAH, can cause serious health issues including cancer, genetic damage, and immune system disruption through both direct exposure and environmental contamination.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: Urban areas are key sources of PAH emissions from traffic and industrial activities, making city air quality and public health a major concern.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: The production and use of materials that emit PAHs necessitate improved industrial practices and regulations to reduce environmental and health risks.
